Cloudflare changelogsUpdates to various Cloudflare productshttps://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/Cloudflare One Client - Cloudflare One Client for macOS (version 2026.8.2100.0)https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-07-warp-macos-ga/https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-07-warp-macos-ga/<p>A new GA release for the macOS Cloudflare One Client is now available on the <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/download/">stable releases downloads page</a>.</p> <p>This release includes the following highlights:</p> <ul> <li>Traffic to split tunnel excluded resources is no longer briefly blocked while the client is connecting or reconnecting. The client now keeps its learned split tunnel configuration across reconnects.</li> <li>Support for routing non-RFC 1918 local IPv4 networks through the tunnel when unrestricted LAN inclusion is enabled by policy or MDM.</li> <li>Faster connects and lower memory use. The hosts file is now read once and shared across the client’s DNS resolvers instead of being reloaded by each one.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Additional changes and improvements</strong></p> <ul> <li>Improved reauthentication reliability and fixed an issue where a reauthentication could force a new registration.</li> <li>Improved client reaction to the current network lowering its MTU.</li> <li>Improved DNS reliability on networks with lower MTUs by clamping the TCP maximum segment size (MSS) for DNS-over-HTTPS connections sent through the tunnel.</li> <li>Individual DNS-over-HTTPS queries now time out instead of hanging when the upstream server stops responding.</li> <li>Improved API reliability by retrying requests dropped when reusing pooled connections.</li> <li>Added an MDM setting to prefer IPv4 when resolving hostnames in proxy mode. The setting is off by default.</li> <li>Fixed the client reconnecting while Emergency Disconnect was active after switching organizations or re-registering.</li> <li>Fixed the client being unable to connect after an upgrade when its stored registration credentials no longer matched its configuration.</li> <li>Fixed the client service restarting unexpectedly when it was slow to respond, such as after waking from sleep.</li> <li>Fixed Extra Logging failing to capture packets across all interfaces.</li> <li>Fixed an issue that could prevent remote diagnostics from completing.</li> <li>Fixed DNS connectivity checks failing on IPv6-only networks.</li> <li>Fixed the client service exiting when its route-monitoring socket was closed after sleep or wake.</li> <li>Fixed DNS enforcement checks making the client service unresponsive on systems with large routing tables.</li> <li>Fixed slow captive portal checks causing the client service to become unresponsive or restart while connecting.</li> <li>Fixed a race when switching tunnel protocols during key rotation that could prevent WireGuard from connecting.</li> <li>Fixed the client continuing to report “No network” after a successful manual disconnect.</li> <li>Fixed a client UI crash that could occur when the daemon connection was reset during an IPC request.</li> <li>Fixed a startup crash when date formatting data for the system locale had not yet loaded.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Known issues</strong></p> <ul> <li>None</li> </ul> Wed, 07 Oct 2026 17:01:53 GMTCloudflare One ClientCloudflare One ClientCloudflare One Client - Cloudflare One Client for Windows (version 2026.8.2100.0)https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-07-warp-windows-ga/https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-07-warp-windows-ga/<p>A new GA release for the Windows Cloudflare One Client is now available on the <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/download/">stable releases downloads page</a>.</p> <p>This release includes the following highlights:</p> <ul> <li>Traffic to split tunnel excluded resources is no longer briefly blocked while the client is connecting or reconnecting. The client now keeps its learned split tunnel configuration across tunnel reconnections.</li> <li>Support for routing non-RFC 1918 local IPv4 networks through the tunnel when unrestricted LAN inclusion is enabled by policy or MDM.</li> <li>Improved connection reliability on devices with very large hosts files. The client now detects a large hosts file, allows more time for its initial DNS check, and shows a banner letting the user know that connecting may take longer.</li> <li>Faster tunnel reconnections and lower memory use. The hosts file is now read once and shared across the client’s DNS resolvers instead of being reloaded by each one.</li> <li>A service recovery mechanism, backed by a Windows scheduled task, now starts the client service on system unlock if it is not already running. This is enabled by default.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Additional changes and improvements</strong></p> <ul> <li>Improved reauthentication reliability and fixed an issue where a reauthentication could force a new registration.</li> <li>Improved client reaction to the current network lowering its MTU.</li> <li>Improved DNS reliability on networks with lower MTUs by clamping the TCP maximum segment size (MSS) for DNS-over-HTTPS connections sent through the tunnel.</li> <li>Individual DNS-over-HTTPS queries now time out instead of hanging when the upstream server stops responding.</li> <li>Improved API reliability by retrying requests dropped when reusing pooled connections.</li> <li>Added an MDM setting to prefer IPv4 when resolving hostnames in proxy mode. The setting is off by default.</li> <li>The client no longer requires the Windows WLAN AutoConfig service to be running.</li> <li>Fixed the client reconnecting while Emergency Disconnect was active after switching organizations or re-registering.</li> <li>Fixed the client being unable to connect after an upgrade when its stored registration credentials no longer matched its configuration.</li> <li>Fixed the client service restarting unexpectedly when it was slow to respond, such as after waking from sleep.</li> <li>Fixed the client service failing to restart after an unexpected termination.</li> <li>Fixed the client UI getting stuck in a connecting state after sleep and wake even though the tunnel was connected.</li> <li>Fixed slow captive portal checks causing the client service to become unresponsive or restart while connecting.</li> <li>Fixed a race when switching tunnel protocols during key rotation that could prevent WireGuard from connecting.</li> <li>Fixed the client continuing to report “No network” after a successful manual disconnect.</li> <li>Fixed Digital Experience Monitoring (DEX) HTTP tests failing TLS validation.</li> <li>Fixed latency spikes and traffic interruptions during TPM-backed API authentication when hardware-backed registration is enabled.</li> <li>Fixed trailing whitespace in BIOS serial numbers causing serial-number and client-certificate device posture checks to fail.</li> <li>Fixed the client UI crashing at startup when it could not write to the Windows registry.</li> <li>Fixed a client UI crash that could occur when the daemon connection was reset during an IPC request.</li> <li>Fixed a startup crash when date formatting data for the system locale had not yet loaded.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Known issues</strong></p> <ul> <li>A Windows DNS client regression may cause connectivity check failures on systems containing large hosts files. While this release includes a fix to mitigate this issue, users may still experience reduced DNS performance and connectivity check failures.</li> </ul> Wed, 07 Oct 2026 17:01:52 GMTCloudflare One ClientCloudflare One ClientCloudflare One Client - Cloudflare One Client for Linux (version 2026.8.2100.0)https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-07-warp-linux-ga/https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-07-warp-linux-ga/<p>A new GA release for the Linux Cloudflare One Client is now available on the <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/download/">stable releases downloads page</a>.</p> <p>This release includes the following highlights:</p> <ul> <li>Traffic to split tunnel excluded resources is no longer briefly blocked while the client is connecting or reconnecting. Local Domain Fallback works as expected in other client modes.</li> </ul> Wed, 07 Oct 2026 16:34:14 GMTCloudflare One ClientCloudflare One ClientLog Explorer - Query Log Explorer datasets from Observability Logshttps://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-07-log-search-in-observability-logs/https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-07-log-search-in-observability-logs/<p>Log Explorer datasets are now queried from the <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/observability/logs/">Logs</a> page under <strong>Observability</strong> in the Cloudflare dashboard. The Logs page brings Log Explorer and Workers Observability datasets together with a shared filter builder, SQL editor, and visualizations.</p> <p>As part of this change, the <strong>Log Explorer</strong> menu is no longer shown in the dashboard navigation.</p> <ul> <li>Your enabled datasets, saved queries, and SQL queries continue to work on the Logs page.</li> <li>To manage datasets, open the dataset selector on the Logs page and select <strong>Configure</strong> next to the Log Explorer datasets.</li> <li>The previous Log Search page remains available at its direct URL.</li> </ul> <p>For more information, refer to <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/log-explorer/log-search/">Log Search</a> and the <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/observability/logs/">Logs overview</a>.</p>Wed, 07 Oct 2026 00:00:00 GMTLog ExplorerLog ExplorerCloudflare Fundamentals, Cloudflare One, Gateway, Organizations - Cloudflare Organizations is generally availablehttps://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-07-organizations-generally-available/https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-07-organizations-generally-available/<p>Cloudflare Organizations is now generally available for Enterprise customers and MSSP/Distributor partners.</p> <p>Organizations provides a top-level container for centrally managing accounts, members, analytics, and shared policies. <p>The strict service token authentication setting applies consistent behavior to requests made with service tokens. When the setting is on for a Zero Trust organization, Access handles requests with service token headers as follows:</p> <ul> <li>If authentication or authorization fails, Access always returns <code>401</code> or <code>403</code> instead of redirecting the client to the login page with <code>302</code>.</li> <li>Only Service Auth policies can authorize the request. Access ignores Allow policies and any <code>CF_Authorization</code> cookie sent with the request.</li> <li>Access does not return a <code>CF_Authorization</code> cookie to the client after successful authentication. Subsequent requests should continue to use service token headers.</li> <li>Failed requests for recognized service tokens appear in <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/insights/logs/dashboard-logs/access-authentication-logs/#non-identity-authentication">Access authentication logs</a>.</li> </ul> <p>Zero Trust organizations created on or after October 5, 2026 have strict service token authentication turned on by default and cannot turn it off. Cloudflare recommends that existing organizations turn it on as well.</p> <p>Organizations created before October 5, 2026 can configure the setting in the dashboard or through the API.</p> <div planhttps://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-02-30-days-analytics-on-every-plan/https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-02-30-days-analytics-on-every-plan/<p>Every plan now gets at least 30 days of analytics data. Adaptive analytics datasets, such as HTTP requests, security events, and DNS analytics, retain at least 31 days of data for Free and Pro domains, and you can query up to 30 days in a single request. Previously, Free and Pro domains could see between 24 hours and 8 days of history depending on the dataset.</p> <p>A full month of history lets you investigate an issue after it happens, compare today with the same day in previous weeks, and tell a one-time spike from a longer trend. The change applies in the Cloudflare dashboard, in <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/analytics/custom-dashboards/">Custom Dashboards</a>, and through the <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/analytics/graphql-api/">GraphQL Analytics API</a>.</p> <p>Domain analytics also now live in one place. In the Cloudflare dashboard, select a domain and go to <strong>Analytics</strong> to see Traffic, Performance, Security, Cache, Origin, DNS, and Visitors as tabs that share one time range and one set of filters. Account-level analytics are under <strong>Observability</strong> &gt; <strong>Analytics</strong>.</p> <p>This change does not alter which datasets or fields your plan can access. Aggregated datasets, such as <code>httpRequests1hGroups</code>, keep their existing per-plan limits. To check the exact retention and query window for a zone or account, query the <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/analytics/graphql-api/features/discovery/settings/">settings</a> for each dataset.</p> <p>For plan-specific limits, refer to <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/waf/analytics/security-analytics/#availability">Security Analytics</a>, <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/waf/analytics/security-events/#availability">Security Events</a>, and <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/analytics/graphql-api/limits/#node-limits-and-availability">GraphQL Analytics API limits</a>.</p>Fri, 02 Oct 2026 00:00:00 GMTAnalyticsAnalyticsAnalytics - Workers Observability logs and traces in Custom Dashboardshttps://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-02-workers-observability-in-custom-dashboards/https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-02-workers-observability-in-custom-dashboards/<p>You can now build Custom Dashboards charts from Workers Observability data. Two new datasets, <strong>Workers Observability — Logs</strong> and <strong>Workers Observability — Traces (OTel)</strong>, let you chart Worker invocations, log levels, errors, CPU and wall time, span counts, and durations next to HTTP traffic, security events, and other analytics datasets.</p> <p>This gives you one dashboard for an application that spans Cloudflare's network and your Workers. For example, you can put request volume, WAF blocks, and Worker error rates on the same view, filter all three by time range, and spot whether a spike in errors lines up with a change in traffic.</p> <p>The datasets are available for every Worker in your account that has <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/logs/workers-logs/">Workers Logs</a> or <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/traces/">Workers Traces</a> turned on. Custom Dashboards also now allow up to 100 dashboards for every account.</p> <p>To get started, refer to <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/analytics/custom-dashboards/#workers-observability-data">Workers Observability data in Custom Dashboards</a>.</p>Fri, 02 Oct 2026 00:00:00 GMTAnalyticsAnalyticsD1 - United States jurisdictionhttps://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-02-us-jurisdiction/https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-02-us-jurisdiction/<p>You can create D1 databases with the <code>us</code> jurisdiction. These databases run and persist data within the United States.</p> <p>Use this option for regional data residency requirements.</p> <p>To create a database with the <code>us</code> jurisdiction, run:</p> <figure class="nb-code-figure" data-nb-lang="sh"><pre class="astro-code astro-code-themes github-light github-dark nb-shiki-c6xiwz" tabindex="0" data-language="sh" data-nb-lang="sh"><code><span class="line"><span class="nb-shiki-1t8gfj">npx</span><span class="nb-shiki-mdbnqw"> wrangler@latest</span><span class="nb-shiki-mdbnqw"> d1</span><span class="nb-shiki-mdbnqw"> create</span><span class="nb-shiki-mdbnqw"> db-with-us-jurisdiction</span><span class="nb-shiki-dzsirb"> \--jurisdiction=us</span></span></code></pre></figure> <p>For more information, refer to <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/configuration/data-location/">D1 data location</a>.</p>Fri, 02 Oct 2026 00:00:00 GMTD1D1Cloudflare Fundamentals, Organizations - Organizations support increased account and zone limitshttps://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-02-organization-account-zone-limits/https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-02-organization-account-zone-limits/<p>Cloudflare Organizations now support up to <strong>20,000 accounts</strong> and <strong>200,000 zones</strong>. For MSSP/Distributors using sub-organizations, these limits are applied at the root Organization.</p> <p>If you require a higher limit, reach out to your account team. The new limits apply to enterprise and MSSP/Distributor Organizations. Legacy reseller partner and brand partner tenants retain their existing quota behavior.</p> <p>For more information, refer to <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/organizations/limitations/#account-and-zone-limits">Account and zone limits</a>.</p>Fri, 02 Oct 2026 00:00:00 GMTCloudflare FundamentalsCloudflare FundamentalsOrganizationsKV - Workers KV namespace jurisdictions are now generally availablehttps://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-02-kv-jurisdictions-ga/https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-02-kv-jurisdictions-ga/<p>Jurisdictions for <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/kv/">Workers KV</a> namespaces are now generally available. When you create a namespace, you can set a <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/kv/reference/data-location/">jurisdiction</a> to make sure the namespace's data is only durably stored within that region. Jurisdictions can help you comply with data localization regulations such as GDPR or FedRAMP. Supported jurisdictions are <code>eu</code>, <code>us</code>, and <code>fedramp</code>.</p> <p>A jurisdiction can only be set when a namespace is created, using the Cloudflare dashboard, Wrangler, the <code>cf</code> CLI, or the REST API, and cannot be added or changed afterwards.</p> <figure class="nb-code-figure" data-nb-lang="sh"><pre class="astro-code astro-code-themes github-light github-dark It hashes fields into an integer within a specified range. Use this result to select a portion of requests.</p> <p>Use <code>cf.random_seed</code> to select approximately 10% of requests at random:</p> <figure class="nb-code-figure" data-nb-lang="txt"><pre class="astro-code astro-code-themes github-light github-dark nb-shiki-c6xiwz" tabindex="0" data-language="txt" data-nb-lang="txt"><code><span class="line"><span class="nb-shiki-wvjl67">hash_in_range(0, 100, cf.random_seed) &lt; 10</span></span></code></pre></figure> <p>With Cloudflare for SaaS, use <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-for-platforms/cloudflare-for-saas/domain-support/custom-metadata/">custom metadata</a> to control rollout progression. Define <code>rollout_pct</code> as a custom key for each hostname. Set its value to an integer from 0 to 100. The expression selects approximately that percentage of requests:</p> <figure class="nb-code-figure" data-nb-lang="txt"><pre class="astro-code astro-code-themes github-light github-dark nb-shiki-c6xiwz" tabindex="0" data-language="txt" data-nb-lang="txt"><code><span class="line"><span class="nb-shiki-wvjl67">hash_in_range(0, 100, cf.random_seed) &lt; coalesce(lookup_json_integer(cf.hostname.metadata, "rollout_pct"), 0)</span></span></code></pre></figure> <p>If <code>rollout_pct</code> is missing, <code>coalesce()</code> supplies <code>0</code>. The rule then matches no requests.</p> <p>For details, refer to the <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/ruleset-engine/rules-language/functions/#hash_in_range"><code>hash_in_range()</code> function reference</a>.</p>Fri, 02 Oct 2026 00:00:00 GMTRulesRulesCloudflare Tunnel - Protect Quick Tunnels with email authenticationhttps://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-02-protected-quick-tunnels/https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-02-protected-quick-tunnels/<p>You can now restrict who can access a <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/tunnel/get-started/quick-tunnels/">Quick Tunnel</a>. Use the new <code>\--allowed-mail</code> flag in <code>cloudflared</code> to require visitors to authenticate with a one-time PIN sent to their email before they reach your local service.</p> <figure class="nb-code-figure" data-nb-lang="sh"><pre class="astro-code astro-code-themes github-light github-dark nb-shiki-c6xiwz" tabindex="0" data-language="sh" data-nb-lang="sh"><code><span class="line"><span class="nb-shiki-1t8gfj">cloudflared</span><span class="nb-shiki-mdbnqw"> tunnel</span><span class="nb-shiki-dzsirb"> \--url</span><span class="nb-shiki-mdbnqw"> http://localhost:8080</span><span class="nb-shiki-dzsirb"> \--allowed-mail</span><span class="nb-shiki-mdbnqw"> alice@example.com</span></span></code></pre></figure> <img src="https://developers.cloudflare.com/cdn-cgi/image/onerror=redirect,width=1512,height=854,format=webp/_astro/protected-quick-tunnels.DlA306r_.gif" alt="Protected Quick Tunnel demo" loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1512" height="854"> <p>Previously, anyone with a <code>trycloudflare.com</code> URL could access the service behind it. Protected Quick Tunnels let you share a local development server, webhook receiver, or demo with specific people without creating a Cloudflare account or configuring a domain.</p> <p>You can allow:</p> <ul> <li>A single email address: <code>\--allowed-mail alice@example.com</code></li> <li>Multiple email addresses, by repeating the flag or using a comma-separated list: <code>\--allowed-mail 'alice@example.com,bob@example.com'</code></li> <li>Every address on a domain: <code>\--allowed-mail '*@example.com'</code></li> </ul> <p>Visitors do not need a Cloudflare account. Access ends for everyone when you stop the <code>cloudflared</code> process.</p> <p>To get started, <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/tunnel/downloads/">update <code>cloudflared</code></a> to the latest version and refer to <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/tunnel/get-started/quick-tunnels/#restrict-access-by-email">Restrict access by email</a>.</p>Fri, 02 Oct 2026 00:00:00 GMTCloudflare TunnelCloudflare TunnelWorkers AI - Introducing Clef: Cloudflare's first open-source decision models, now on Workers AIhttps://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-01-clef-workers-ai/https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-01-clef-workers-ai/ <p>Meet <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/models/clef/"><code>@cf/cloudflare/clef</code></a> and <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/models/clef-flash/"><code>@cf/cloudflare/clef-flash</code></a>, the first models trained by the Cloudflare Workers AI team, available on Workers AI today.</p> <p>Clef is a decision model, in the same family as <a href="https://typesafe.ai/blog/introducing-system-one-models-and-jev" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Typesafe's Jev<span class="external-link"> ↗︎</span></a>. Instead of generating text, it reads an input state and a set of typed questions, then returns a probability for every allowed answer. Your agent gets a structured decision it can act on immediately, for example: route the ticket, block the request, or escalate to a human. There is no free-form output to parse and no reasoning tokens to wait for.</p> <p>Both models are hosted on Workers AI as <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/models/clef/">Clef</a> and <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/models/clef-flash/">Clef-flash</a>. We are also open-sourcing the weights under the Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face: <a href="https://huggingface.co/Cloudflare/clef" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Clef<span class="external-link"> ↗︎</span></a> and <a href="https://huggingface.co/Cloudflare/clef-flash" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Clef-flash<span class="external-link"> ↗︎</span></a>. Read the <a href="https://blog.cloudflare.com/clef-decision-models/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">launch blog post<span class="external-link"> ↗︎</span></a> for the full story, including how we trained them.</p> <p>We are also launching a reinforcement learning (RL) fine-tuning service to help you tune Clef for your own workloads. <a href="https://www.cloudflare.com/resource/clef-rl-interest" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Sign up to work with us as a design partner<span class="external-link"> ↗︎</span></a>.</p> <div tabindex="-1" class="heading-wrapper level-h4"><h4 id="built-for-the-hot-path">Built for the hot path</h4><a class="anchor-link" href="#built-for-the-hot-path"><span aria-hidden="true" class="anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path fill="currentcolor" d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42Zm8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33ZM8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 1.1.22 1 1 0 0 0 .32-.22l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42Z"></path></svg></span></a></div> <p>Clef is designed to be fast so decisions come back in milliseconds. Across our 43 benchmark runs, we achieved speeds where Clef is 2.5x faster than Jev at the median, and Clef-flash 13x faster.</p> <div class="table-scroll" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Table"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Latency</th> <th>Clef</th> <th>Clef-flash</th> <th>Jev</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>Median</td> <td>209.3 ms</td> <td><strong>38.8 ms</strong></td> <td>524.1 ms</td> </tr> <tr> <td>p95</td> <td>238.6 ms</td> <td><strong>122.4 ms</strong></td> <td>536.0 ms</td> </tr> </tbody> </table></div> <p>Hosting on Workers AI adds to that speed. Requests run on GPUs across Cloudflare's network, running close to your users, so the network round trip stays short. You can put Clef directly in the request path of your agent, then hand off to an LLM on Workers AI to take action.</p> <div tabindex="-1" class="heading-wrapper level-h4"><h4 id="leading-the-benchmarks">Leading the benchmarks</h4><a class="anchor-link" href="#leading-the-benchmarks"><span aria-hidden="true" class="anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path fill="currentcolor" d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42Zm8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33ZM8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 1.1.22 1 1 0 0 0 .32-.22l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42Z"></path></svg></span></a></div> <p>Across 10 decision benchmarks, a Clef model scores highest on 7, ahead of Jev and other open decision models. A few highlights:</p> <div class="table-scroll" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Table"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Benchmark</th> <th>Clef</th> <th>Clef-flash</th> <th>Jev</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>BFCL (case exact)</td> <td>98.47</td> <td><strong>98.76</strong></td> <td>95.75</td> </tr> <tr> <td>BANKING77 (macro-F1)</td> <td><strong>94.20</strong></td> <td>90.93</td> <td>79.74</td> </tr> <tr> <td>CLINC150+OOS (macro-F1)</td> <td><strong>97.43</strong></td> <td>66.77</td> <td>89.27</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Home appliances (case exact)</td> <td>82.95</td> <td><strong>97.73</strong></td> <td>52.27</td> </tr> </tbody> </table></div> <p>On Typesafe's own workflow evals, Clef beats Jev in 3 of 4 areas: invoice processing, customer service, and security incidents. The full results are on the <a href="https://huggingface.co/Cloudflare/clef" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Hugging Face model card<span class="external-link"> ↗︎</span></a>.</p> <div tabindex="-1" class="heading-wrapper level-h4"><h4 id="drop-in-compatible-with-jev">Drop-in compatible with Jev</h4><a class="anchor-link" href="#drop-in-compatible-with-jev"><span aria-hidden="true" class="anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path fill="currentcolor" d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42Zm8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33ZM8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 1.1.22 1 1 0 0 0 .32-.22l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42Z"></path></svg></span></a></div> <div class="table-scroll" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Table"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Model</th> <th>Size</th> <th>Best for</th> <th>Context window</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/models/clef/"><code>@cf/cloudflare/clef</code></a></td> <td>27B</td> <td>Highest-precision decisions</td> <td>64K tokens</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/models/clef-flash/"><code>@cf/cloudflare/clef-flash</code></a></td> <td>9B</td> <td>Latency-critical, hot-path decisions</td> <td>64K tokens</td> </tr> </tbody> </table></div> <p>Clef follows the System One API, so you can switch an existing Jev integration to Clef by changing the endpoint and model. Ask up to 64 questions per request, in three types:</p> <ul> <li><strong><code>noul</code></strong>: A yes/no question. Returns the probability that the answer is yes.</li> <li><strong><code>choice</code></strong>: Pick one option from a set you define. Returns the chosen option, a probability per option, and a confidence value.</li> <li><strong><code>score</code></strong>: Rate against an ordered rubric. Returns a probability-weighted score and a probability per level.</li> </ul> <div><div data-nb-tabs data-nb-sync-key="workersExamples" class><div class="relative flex border-b border-border" human in the loop.</li> <li><strong>Threat intelligence</strong>: Classify a website by category. Paired with <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/browser-run/">Browser Run</a>, Clef fetched, rendered, and classified a domain in 2.2 seconds, compared to 4.7 seconds for <code>gpt-oss-120b</code> in the same workflow.</li> <li><strong>Trust and safety</strong>: Score user submissions against your own policy rubric and act on the probability.</li> <li><strong>Agent guardrails</strong>: Let an agent check "should I take this action?" in tens of milliseconds before calling a tool.</li> <li><strong>Visual classification</strong>: Pass up to four images alongside the state. Unlike text-only decision models, Clef has a vision encoder.</li> </ul> <div tabindex="-1" class="heading-wrapper level-h4"><h4 id="get-started">Get started</h4><a class="anchor-link" href="#get-started"><span aria-hidden="true" class="anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path fill="currentcolor" d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42Zm8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33ZM8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 1.1.22 1 1 0 0 0 .32-.22l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42Z"></path></svg></span></a></div> <p>Use Clef through the <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/configuration/bindings/">Workers AI binding</a> (<code>env.AI.run()</code>) or the REST API at <code>/ai/run</code>. You can also use <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/">AI Gateway</a> with these endpoints.</p> <p>For more information, refer to the <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/models/clef/">Clef model page</a>, the <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/models/clef-flash/">Clef-flash model page</a>, and <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/platform/pricing/">pricing</a>.</p>Thu, 01 Oct 2026 13:00:00 GMTWorkers AIWorkers AIAgents, Workers - The best way to do MCP auth just got better: Workers OAuth Provider goes v1, with a new split API and full support for MCP 2026-07-28https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-01-workers-oauth-provider-1x/https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-01-workers-oauth-provider-1x/ <p><a href="https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider" target="_blank" rel="noopener"><code>@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider</code><span class="external-link"> ↗︎</span></a> is now v1, with a new split API. One Worker acts as the authorization server: it signs users in and issues tokens. Your MCP server acts as the resource server, and can run in another Worker. It validates each token with the authorization server over a <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/bindings/service-bindings/">Service Binding</a>, without crossing the public Internet.</p> <ul> <li>It supports the <a href="https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization" target="_blank" rel="noopener">MCP 2026-07-28 authorization specification<span class="external-link"> ↗︎</span></a>, including <a href="https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider/blob/main/docs/authorization-server.md#client-id-metadata-documents" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Client ID Metadata Documents<span class="external-link"> ↗︎</span></a> and <a href="https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider/blob/main/docs/authorization-server.md#authorization-response-issuer" target="_blank" rel="noopener">issuer identification<span class="external-link"> ↗︎</span></a>. It still works with older clients, including those using <a href="https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider/blob/main/docs/authorization-server.md#dynamic-client-registration" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Dynamic Client Registration<span class="external-link"> ↗︎</span></a>.</li> <li><code>insufficientScope()</code> gives you <a href="https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider/blob/main/docs/authorization-server.md#scopes-and-step-up-authorization" target="_blank" rel="noopener">step-up authorization<span class="external-link"> ↗︎</span></a> in one line.</li> <li>The authorization server and the resource server can run in <a href="https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider/blob/main/docs/resource-servers.md#separate-workers" target="_blank" rel="noopener">different Workers<span class="external-link"> ↗︎</span></a> with different <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/waf/">WAF</a> and <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/waf/rate-limiting-rules/">rate limiting</a> rules.</li> <li>One authorization server can issue tokens for <a href="https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider/blob/main/docs/authorization-server.md#resources-and-token-audiences" target="_blank" rel="noopener">many MCP servers<span class="external-link"> ↗︎</span></a>.</li> <li>A <a href="https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider/blob/main/skills/migrate-to-1.0/SKILL.md" <p><code>OAuthResourceServer</code> publishes the <a href="https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9728" target="_blank" rel="noopener">RFC 9728<span class="external-link"> ↗︎</span></a> protected resource metadata that MCP clients use to find your authorization server. It answers requests without a token with a <code>401</code> challenge that points to that metadata. It also rejects tokens issued for any other resource.</p> <p>You can still use <code>OAuthProvider</code> as both the authorization server and the MCP server. For most 0.x deployments, the only required change is to add <code>resourceMetadata: { resource }</code>.</p> <div tabindex="-1" class="heading-wrapper level-h4"><h4 availablehttps://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-01-ai-search-generally-available/https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-01-ai-search-generally-available/<p>AI Search is now generally available. Usage-based billing begins on November 1, 2026, with included monthly ingestion, storage, semantic query, and full-text query usage. Cloudflare will send a reminder email the week before billing begins.</p> <p>Refer to <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-search/platform/limits-pricing/">Limits &amp; pricing</a> for rates and included usage.</p> <div tabindex="-1" class="heading-wrapper level-h4"><h4 id="hybrid-search-is-on-by-default">Hybrid search is on by default</h4><a class="anchor-link" href="#hybrid-search-is-on-by-default"><span aria-hidden="true" class="anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path fill="currentcolor" d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42Zm8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33ZM8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 1.1.22 1 1 0 0 0 .32-.22l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42Z"></path></svg></span></a></div> <p>New AI Search instances use hybrid search by default. Hybrid search combines semantic vector retrieval with full-text matching. You can choose a different index method when you create an instance.</p> <p>Refer to <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-search/configuration/indexing/hybrid-search/">Hybrid search</a> for details.</p> <div tabindex="-1" class="heading-wrapper level-h4"><h4 id="workers-ai-embeddings-and-reranking-are-included">Workers AI embeddings and reranking are included</h4><a class="anchor-link" href="#workers-ai-embeddings-and-reranking-are-included"><span aria-hidden="true" class="anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path fill="currentcolor" d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42Zm8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33ZM8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 1.1.22 1 1 0 0 0 .32-.22l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42Z"></path></svg></span></a></div> <p>Workers AI embedding and reranking calls made by AI Search are included in AI Search pricing. These calls no longer appear on your Workers AI bill or in your AI Gateway logs. Generation, query rewriting, and external providers continue to use your account and gateway.</p> <p>Refer to <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-search/platform/limits-pricing/">Limits &amp; pricing</a> for details.</p> <div tabindex="-1" class="heading-wrapper level-h4"><h4 id="multimodal-model-and-image-support">Multimodal model and image support</h4><a class="anchor-link" href="#multimodal-model-and-image-support"><span aria-hidden="true" class="anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path fill="currentcolor" d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42Zm8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33ZM8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 1.1.22 1 1 0 0 0 .32-.22l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42Z"></path></svg></span></a></div> <p>AI Search supports the <code>@cf/qwen/qwen3-vl-embedding-2b</code> and <code>google-ai-studio/gemini-embedding-2</code> multimodal embedding models. Search and chat requests can include images through the REST API and public endpoint.</p> <p>Refer to <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-search/configuration/models/supported-models/">Supported models</a> for the full list of embedding models.</p> <div tabindex="-1" class="heading-wrapper level-h4"><h4 id="ocr-availability-and-increased-file-limits">OCR availability and increased file limits</h4><a class="anchor-link" href="#ocr-availability-and-increased-file-limits"><span aria-hidden="true" class="anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path fill="currentcolor" d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42Zm8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33ZM8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 1.1.22 1 1 0 0 0 .32-.22l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42Z"></path></svg></span></a></div> <p>Optical character recognition (OCR) is available on every account for scanned PDFs. Plain-text or code files and PDFs with OCR enabled can be up to 10 MiB. PDFs without OCR and other supported formats remain limited to 4 MiB.</p> <p>Refer to <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-search/configuration/data-source/#file-limits">Data source</a> for file limits and <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-search/platform/limits-pricing/">Limits &amp; pricing</a> for OCR pricing.</p> <div tabindex="-1" class="heading-wrapper level-h4"><h4 id="source-type-inference">Source type inference</h4><a class="anchor-link" href="#source-type-inference"><span aria-hidden="true" class="anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path fill="currentcolor" d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42Zm8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33ZM8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 1.1.22 1 1 0 0 0 .32-.22l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42Z"></path></svg></span></a></div> <p>When you create an AI Search instance, the <code>type</code> field is optional. AI Search infers a website source from an HTTP or HTTPS URL, or an R2 source from an existing bucket name.</p> <p>Refer to <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-search/configuration/data-source/">Data source</a> for details.</p>Thu, 01 Oct 2026 00:00:00 GMTAI SearchAI SearchArtifacts, Workers - Artifacts is now in open betahttps://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-01-artifacts-open-beta/https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-01-artifacts-open-beta/<p><a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/artifacts/">Artifacts</a>, Cloudflare's versioned file system that speaks Git, is now in open beta. Artifacts is built for scale, so you can create a repository per project, user, session, or task.</p> <p>With Artifacts, you can:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Deploy repositories to Workers</strong> — Connect an Artifacts repository through <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/ci-cd/builds/git-integration/artifacts-integration/">Workers Builds</a>. Pushes to the production branch deploy the updated Worker, while other branches create or update <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/previews/">Worker Previews</a>.</li> <li><strong>Programmatically manage repositories</strong> — Use an <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/artifacts/api/workers-binding/">Artifacts binding</a> from a Worker to create or fork repos, inspect files and commits, read files by path, and issue repo-scoped Git tokens.</li> <li><strong>React to repository changes</strong> — <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/artifacts/guides/event-subscriptions/">Subscribe to events</a> when a repository is created, imported, forked, deleted, pushed to, cloned, or fetched.</li> <li><strong>Control where repository data is stored</strong> — Choose to <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/artifacts/guides/data-localization/">store and process</a> your data in the US or EU.</li> <li><strong>Monitor repository usage</strong> — View total operations, pulls, pushes, errors, and error rates in the Cloudflare dashboard or <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/artifacts/observability/metrics/">via API for analytics</a>.</li> </ul> <p>Artifacts is available for customers on the Workers Paid plan. Cloudflare will begin <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/artifacts/platform/pricing/">billing</a> for Artifacts on October 14, 2026.</p> <div tabindex="-1" class="heading-wrapper level-h4"><h4 id="build-the-next-github-on-cloudflare">Build the next GitHub on Cloudflare</h4><a class="anchor-link" href="#build-the-next-github-on-cloudflare"><span aria-hidden="true" class="anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path fill="currentcolor" d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42Zm8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33ZM8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 1.1.22 1 1 0 0 0 .32-.22l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42Z"></path></svg></span></a></div> <p>We are hosting a competition to see who can build the next GitHub on Cloudflare using Workers and Artifacts.</p> <p><a href="https://www.cloudflare.com/git-competition/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Apply today<span class="external-link"> ↗︎</span></a> — submissions are open until October 14, 2026.</p> <p>The first-place team will receive $25,000 in Cloudflare credits. The top three teams will be flown to San Francisco to present what they built at Cloudflare Connect.</p> <p>Get started with the <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/artifacts/">Artifacts documentation</a>.</p>Thu, 01 Oct 2026 00:00:00 GMTArtifactsArtifactsWorkersBasin Pipelines, Basin - Basin Pipelines ingest limit increased to 1 GB/shttps://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-01-stream-ingest-limit-increase/https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-01-stream-ingest-limit-increase/<p>Each <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/basin-pipelines/streams/">Basin Pipelines stream</a> can now ingest up to 1 GB/s, increased from 5 MB/s.</p> <p>The higher per-stream limit gives high-volume application events, telemetry, and logs more room to grow without splitting ingestion across streams solely to stay within the previous limit.</p> <p>For the full list of stream, sink, and pipeline limits, refer to <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/basin-pipelines/platform/limits/">Basin Pipelines limits</a>.</p>Thu, 01 Oct 2026 00:00:00 GMTBasin PipelinesBasin PipelinesBasinBasin, Basin Pipelines, Basin Catalog, Basin SQL - Cloudflare Basin is now generally availablehttps://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-01-basin-ga/https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-01-basin-ga/ <p><a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/basin/">Basin</a>, formerly the Cloudflare Data Platform, is now generally available. Basin brings an end-to-end analytics platform to the Developer Platform, enabling you to collect data from a variety of sources, such as apps, infrastructure, devices, and other Cloudflare services, then query it to answer analytical questions.</p> <div tabindex="-1" class="heading-wrapper level-h4"><h4 id="basin-pipelines">Basin Pipelines</h4><a class="anchor-link" href="#basin-pipelines"><span aria-hidden="true" class="anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path fill="currentcolor" d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42Zm8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33ZM8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 1.1.22 1 1 0 0 0 .32-.22l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42Z"></path></svg></span></a></div> <p><a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/basin-pipelines/">Basin Pipelines</a>, formerly Cloudflare Pipelines, ingests events from Workers, HTTP endpoints, and Cloudflare <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/logpush/">Logpush</a>. It transforms events with SQL and ingests them into Iceberg tables or files on R2. With Basin Pipelines you can:</p> <ul> <li>Ingest application and device events through HTTP endpoints or Workers bindings.</li> <li>Filter and reshape Cloudflare logs before storing them as Iceberg tables, Parquet, or JSON.</li> <li>Catch schema mismatches with typed bindings and investigate dropped events in the dashboard.</li> </ul> <div tabindex="-1" class="heading-wrapper level-h4"><h4 id="basin-catalog">Basin Catalog</h4><a class="anchor-link" href="#basin-catalog"><span aria-hidden="true" class="anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path fill="currentcolor" d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42Zm8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33ZM8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 1.1.22 1 1 0 0 0 .32-.22l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42Z"></path></svg></span></a></div> <p><a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/basin-catalog/">Basin Catalog</a>, formerly R2 Data Catalog, manages and automatically maintains <a href="https://iceberg.apache.org/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Apache Iceberg tables<span class="external-link"> ↗︎</span></a> to keep them fast, cost-efficient, and accessible to any compatible query engine. With Basin Catalog you can:</p> <ul> <li>Connect DuckDB, Spark, Snowflake, or PyIceberg to the same tables.</li> <li>Maintain growing tables with compaction, snapshot expiration, and manifest optimization.</li> <li>Share analytical data across tools and clouds without paying egress fees.</li> </ul> <div tabindex="-1" class="heading-wrapper level-h4"><h4 id="basin-sql">Basin SQL</h4><a class="anchor-link" href="#basin-sql"><span aria-hidden="true" class="anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path fill="currentcolor" d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42Zm8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33ZM8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 1.1.22 1 1 0 0 0 .32-.22l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42Z"></path></svg></span></a></div> <p><a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/basin-sql/">Basin SQL</a>, formerly R2 SQL, is a serverless, distributed SQL engine for querying large Apache Iceberg tables in Basin Catalog without managing or scaling compute. With Basin SQL you can:</p> <ul> <li>Summarize and rank data with standard and approximate aggregates, grouping sets, and window functions.</li> <li>Combine and inspect datasets with joins, subqueries, common table expressions, set operations, schema discovery, and <code>EXPLAIN</code>.</li> <li>Transform strings, timestamps, JSON, and complex values with more than 190 functions.</li> </ul> <div tabindex="-1" class="heading-wrapper level-h4"><h4 id="get-started">Get started</h4><a class="anchor-link" href="#get-started"><span aria-hidden="true" class="anchor-icon"><svg width="16" Infrastructurehttps://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-01-infrastructure-target-tag-permissions/https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-01-infrastructure-target-tag-permissions/<p>You can now tag <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/applications/non-http/infrastructure-apps/#tag-targets">targets</a> using only the <code>Zero Trust Write</code> API token permission. Previously, tagging targets through the API required both <code>Zero Trust Write</code> and <code>Tag Write</code> permissions on the API token.</p> <p>This change applies to inline target tagging through the <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/zero_trust/subresources/access/subresources/infrastructure/subresources/targets/">Infrastructure Access Targets API</a>. Tagging resources through the general <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/resource-tagging/">Resource Tagging API</a> still requires the <code>Tag Admin</code>, <code>Tag Write</code>, or equivalent role.</p> <p>For more information, refer to <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/access-controls/applications/non-http/infrastructure-apps/#tag-targets">Tag targets</a>.</p>Thu, 01 Oct 2026 00:00:00 GMTCloudflare OneCloudflare OneAccessDurable Objects - Pending I/O operations allow Durable Objects to continue long-running work without a connected clienthttps://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-01-pending-io-keep-alive/https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-01-pending-io-keep-alive/<p>Durable Objects remain active while handling a request from a connected client. This change applies when no client is connected, such as when an agent continues a submitted job after its client disconnects.</p> <p>This behavior is the default for Workers with a compatibility date of <code>2026-10-01</code> or later. To use it with an earlier date, add the <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/compatibility-flags/#durable-object-io-tasks-prevent-eviction"><code>durable_object_io_tasks_prevent_eviction</code></a> compatibility flag. To opt out, add the <code>durable_object_io_tasks_do_not_prevent_eviction</code> flag.</p> <p>Pending <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/bindings/service-bindings/">service binding</a> requests now keep Durable Objects running while they wait for a response. Pending calls to another Durable Object through remote procedure call (RPC) or <code>fetch()</code>, as well as <code>this.ctx.container.monitor()</code>, now also keep the Durable Object running.</p> <p>Promises passed to <code>this.ctx.waitUntil()</code> and pending <code>setTimeout()</code> and <code>setInterval()</code> timers also receive this protection.</p> <p>Previously, Cloudflare could shut down an idle Durable Object while one of these operations remained pending without a connected client. This could stop unfinished work.</p> <p>This change helps you run long-running tasks such as agents. An agent can call tools through service bindings, coordinate with other Durable Objects, or wait for a container process without relying on the original client to remain connected.</p> <p>Outbound <code>fetch()</code> requests to external services, TCP sockets, and outbound WebSockets already keep Durable Objects running.</p> <p>Each pending operation prevents idle shutdown for up to 15 minutes. Starting another one later can extend the Durable Object's time in memory. The limit applies to each operation, not to the total time in memory.</p> <img src="https://developers.cloudflare.com/cdn-cgi/image/onerror=redirect,width=820,height=360,format=svg/_astro/pending-io-keep-alive.vVfDqYTX.svg" alt="Timeline of a service binding fetch, an RPC call, and monitor() each preventing eviction for up to 15 minutes" loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="820" height="360"> <p>Duration charges continue while an operation prevents eviction.</p> <p>For more information, refer to <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/concepts/durable-object-lifecycle/">Lifecycle of a Durable Object</a>.</p>Thu, 01 Oct 2026 00:00:00 GMTDurable ObjectsDurable ObjectsCloudflare Fundamentals - Account members can self-serve create Account API tokenshttps://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-01-account-api-token-provisioning/https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-01-account-api-token-provisioning/<p>Account API token creation is no longer limited to Super Administrators. Members with the <strong>API Token Provisioning</strong> role can now create Account API tokens via the Dashboard, API, Terraform, or CF CLI, making it easier for developers and platform teams to provision credentials without depending on a Super Administrator for Account API Token Provisioning.</p> <img src="https://developers.cloudflare.com/cdn-cgi/image/onerror=redirect,width=1540,height=818,format=webp/_astro/2026-10-01-account-api-token-provisioning.Dn0G5DUa.png" alt="Creating an Account API Token via CF CLI" loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1540" height="818"> <div tabindex="-1" class="heading-wrapper level-h4"><h4 id="whats-new">What's new</h4><a class="anchor-link" href="#whats-new"><span aria-hidden="true" class="anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path fill="currentcolor" d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42Zm8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33ZM8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 1.1.22 1 1 0 0 0 .32-.22l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42Z"></path></svg></span></a></div> <ul> <li><strong>Delegated creation</strong>: Members with the <strong>API Token Provisioning</strong> role can create Account API tokens from the dashboard. Administrators can grant this role through the dashboard, API, or Terraform.</li> <li><strong>OAuth support for token creation</strong>: OAuth clients that request the <code>account_api_tokens:create</code> scope, starting with Cloudflare CLI, can create Account API tokens.</li> <li><strong>Account API token permissions limited to the creator’s access at creation time</strong>: Members can only create an Account API Token using the permissions they already have. For OAuth-created tokens, permissions are also limited to the scopes granted during authorization.</li> <li><strong>Creator attribution and visibility</strong>: Account API tokens now include creator metadata. Super Administrators and Administrators can view all Account API tokens in an account, while members with the <strong>API Token Provisioning</strong> role can only view tokens they created.</li> </ul> <p>For more information, refer to <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/api/get-started/account-owned-tokens/">Account API tokens</a>, <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/api/how-to/create-via-api/">Create tokens via API</a>, and <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/manage-members/roles/">Roles</a>.</p>Thu, 01 Oct 2026 00:00:00 GMTCloudflare FundamentalsCloudflare FundamentalsRules - Handle missing values with coalesce()https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-01-coalesce-function/https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-10-01-coalesce-function/<p>The <code>coalesce()</code> function returns the first argument that is not nil. Your own Durable Object class now controls each sandbox container directly, through the <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/api/durable-object-container/">Durable Object container API</a> on <code>this.ctx.container</code>.</p> <p>With 1.0, your class can:</p> <ul> <li>Choose the image and instance size each time it starts a sandbox. One class can run sandboxes on different images, and a deploy does not restart sandboxes that are running.</li> <li>Save the files of a sandbox as a <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/sandbox/files/save-and-restore-a-workspace/">snapshot</a>, in public beta, and start the same sandbox or a new one from it.</li> <li>Decide when each sandbox stops, for example when a task finishes, when its user goes idle, or after it saves a snapshot.</li> <li>Run commands with streamed input and output, send them signals, and open <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/sandbox/commands/open-a-terminal-in-the-browser/">terminals</a>.</li> <li>Serve <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/sandbox/previews/">previews</a> from ports in the sandbox, with your own hostnames and authentication.</li> <li>Handle outbound requests for each hostname in Worker code, so <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/sandbox/network/call-an-authenticated-api/">credentials</a> and bindings stay in your Worker.</li> <li>Expose only the methods that you want callers to use.</li> <li>Run an <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/tools/sandbox/">agent</a> in the same Durable Object, and give the model a tool that runs commands in the sandbox.</li> </ul> container API directly, with the <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-09-30-durable-object-scheduling-policy/"><code>durable_object</code> scheduling policy</a> and <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-09-30-snapshots/">container snapshots</a>, both in public beta. <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/sandbox/reference/"><code>@cloudflare/sandbox</code></a> adds classes for work that the API does not include:</p> <ul> <li><code>Files</code> streams files in and out of the running sandbox.</li> <li><code>S3Mount</code> mounts an S3-compatible bucket, such as R2. Your Worker signs each storage request, so the credentials stay out of the sandbox.</li> <li><code>DirectoryBackup</code> saves a directory to R2 and restores it into any sandbox, including one on a newer image.</li> </ul> <div tabindex="-1" class="heading-wrapper level-h4"><h4 id="if-you-use-sandbox-sdk-0x">If you use Sandbox SDK 0.x</h4><a class="anchor-link" href="#if-you-use-sandbox-sdk-0x"><span aria-hidden="true" class="anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path fill="currentcolor" d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42Zm8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33ZM8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 1.1.22 1 1 0 0 0 .32-.22l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42Z"></path></svg></span></a></div> <p>Your 0.x applications keep running, and <code>@cloudflare/sandbox</code> 0.x stays on npm. Sandbox SDK 0.x receives bug and security fixes until 2026-12-31, and its documentation stays at <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/sandbox/sdk/">Sandbox SDK 0.x</a>.</p> <p>When you are ready, <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/sandbox/sdk/migrate/">Migrate from Sandbox SDK 0.x</a> shows the 1.0 code for each 0.x feature, including preview URLs, tunnels, background processes, terminals, backups, and the code interpreter. The guide keeps the preview URLs and named tunnels that your 0.x application created working. You can move every sandbox in one deploy, or run a 1.0 class next to your 0.x class and move sandboxes one at a time. The deploy that moves an existing class to the new policy is one-way, so the guide shows how to rehearse it first.</p> <p>The <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/sandbox/">Sandboxes for Windows (version 2026.8.2033.1)https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-09-30-warp-windows-beta/https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-09-30-warp-windows-beta/<p>A new Beta release for the Windows Cloudflare One Client is now available on the <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/download/beta-releases/">beta releases downloads page</a>.</p> <p>This beta release includes the following changes and improvements:</p> <ul> <li>Fixed an issue that could briefly block traffic to split tunnel excluded resources while the client was connecting or reconnecting.</li> <li>Improved reauthentication reliability and fixed an issue where a reauthentication could force a new registration.</li> <li>Improved client reaction to the current network lowering its MTU.</li> <li>Added support for routing non-RFC 1918 local IPv4 networks through the WARP tunnel when unrestricted LAN inclusion is enabled by policy or MDM.</li> <li>Improved DNS reliability on networks with lower MTUs by clamping the TCP maximum segment size (MSS) for DNS-over-HTTPS connections sent through the tunnel.</li> <li>Improved API reliability by retrying requests dropped when reusing pooled connections.</li> <li>The client no longer requires the Windows WLAN AutoConfig service to be running.</li> <li>Implemented a service recovery mechanism backed by Windows scheduler task to start WARP service on system unlock if not already started.</li> <li>Fixed slow captive portal checks causing the client service to become unresponsive or restart while connecting.</li> <li>Fixed a race when switching tunnel protocols during key rotation that could prevent WireGuard from connecting.</li> <li>Fixed the client continuing to report 'No network' after a successful manual disconnect.</li> <li>Fixed Digital Experience Monitoring (DEX) HTTP tests failing TLS validation on Windows.</li> <li>Fixed the client UI crashing at startup when it could not write to the Windows registry.</li> <li>Fixed latency spikes and traffic interruptions during TPM-backed API authentication when hardware-backed registration is enabled.</li> <li>Fixed trailing whitespace in BIOS serial numbers causing serial-number and client-certificate device posture checks to fail.</li> <li>Fixed a client UI crash that could occur when the daemon connection was reset during an IPC request.</li> <li>Fixed a after a successful manual disconnect.</li> <li>Fixed Digital Experience Monitoring (DEX) HTTP tests failing TLS validation on Windows.</li> <li>Fixed the client UI crashing at startup when it could not write to the Windows registry.</li> <li>Fixed latency spikes and traffic interruptions during TPM-backed API authentication when hardware-backed registration is enabled.</li> <li>Fixed trailing whitespace in BIOS serial numbers causing serial-number and client-certificate device posture checks to fail.</li> <li>Fixed a client UI crash that could occur when the daemon connection was reset It shows what users and agents are doing with AI, and where a selected model may be more capable than a task requires.</p> <p>On the analysis side, User Insights groups conversations by task, tracks conversation turns, and helps you compare model fit with cost and latency.</p> <img src="https://developers.cloudflare.com/cdn-cgi/image/onerror=redirect,width=1434,height=606,format=webp/_astro/user-insights-task-analysis.CS2pm7wg.png" alt="User Insights task and model analysis grouped by task categories" loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1434" height="606"> <p>The Potential Savings view highlights requests that may work with faster or less expensive models without compromising output quality. These are the same signals that Cloudflare's <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/features/auto-router/">Auto Router</a> uses to select a model based on task and cost.</p> <img src="https://developers.cloudflare.com/cdn-cgi/image/onerror=redirect,width=1506,height=669,format=webp/_astro/user-insights-potential-savings.C7j_Gjcn.png" alt="Potential Savings view comparing tasks and suggested models" loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1506" height="669"> <p>These new insights are available to all AI Gateway customers at no additional cost. For more information, refer to <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-gateway/observability/user-insights/">User Insights</a>.</p>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 00:00:00 GMTAI GatewayAI GatewayBrowser Run - Connect multiple clients to one Browser Run sessionhttps://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-09-29-concurrent-session-connections/https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-09-29-concurrent-session-connections/ <p><a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/browser-run/">Browser Run</a> sessions now accept multiple concurrent connections. href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/">Containers</a> custom instance types no longer limit disk based on memory. Previously, a custom instance type could have a maximum of 2 GB of disk for each 1 GiB of memory. You can now allocate up to the 20 GB disk maximum to any custom instance type.</p> <p>Use this to run workloads that need more disk than memory, such as workloads with large container images, datasets, or build caches. The maximum image size is the same as the instance disk space, so more disk also lets you deploy larger images.</p> <p>For example, a custom instance type with 1 vCPU and 3 GiB of memory was previously limited to 6 GB of disk. For the full list, refer to <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/containers/platform/limits/#custom-instance-types">Custom Instance Types</a>.</p>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 00:00:00 GMTContainersContainersCloudflare Mesh, Cloudflare Tunnel, Cloudflare One, Gateway, Workers VPC - Identify Mesh, Workers VPC, and Cloudflare Tunnel replicas in network logshttps://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-09-29-mesh-workers-vpc-network-logs/https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-09-29-mesh-workers-vpc-network-logs/<p>You can now tell a person on a laptop apart from a Mesh node or an AI agent running on Workers, without matching on connector email addresses or Mesh IP ranges — and see exactly which Cloudflare Tunnel and <code>cloudflared</code> replica received each session.</p> <p><a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/insights/logs/dashboard-logs/gateway-logs/#network-logs">Gateway network logs</a> and <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/logs/logpush/logpush-job/datasets/account/zero_trust_network_sessions/">Zero Trust Network Session Logs</a> now identify two new kinds of traffic:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Mesh</strong> — Traffic sent from or delivered to a <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/mesh/">Cloudflare Mesh</a> node. Previously, Mesh nodes were logged the same way as devices running the <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/team-and-resources/devices/cloudflare-one-client/">Cloudflare One Client</a>, because Mesh nodes run the client in headless mode.</li> <li><strong>Workers VPC</strong> — Traffic sent by a Worker through a <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-vpc/">Workers VPC</a> binding. Previously, Workers VPC sessions were not recorded in Network Session Logs.</li> </ul> <img src="https://developers.cloudflare.com/cdn-cgi/image/onerror=redirect,width=1439,height=796,format=webp/_astro/2026-09-28-mesh-workers-vpc-network-logs.iGvLKYk7.gif" alt="Viewing Mesh and Workers VPC traffic in Gateway network logs" loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1439" height="796"> <div tabindex="-1" class="heading-wrapper level-h4"><h4 id="gateway-network-logs">Gateway network logs</h4><a class="anchor-link" href="#gateway-network-logs"><span aria-hidden="true" class="anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path fill="currentcolor" d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42Zm8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33ZM8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 1.1.22 1 1 0 0 0 .32-.22l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42Z"></path></svg></span></a></div> <p>To view these values in the dashboard, go to <strong>Zero Trust</strong> &gt; <strong>Insights &amp; Logs</strong> &gt; <strong>Logs</strong> &gt; <strong>Network logs</strong>, select <strong>Columns</strong>, and turn on <strong>Traffic Source</strong> and <strong>Traffic Destination</strong>. Both values also appear under <strong>Network query details</strong> when you open a log entry.</p> <div tabindex="-1" class="heading-wrapper level-h4"><h4 id="network-session-logs">Network Session Logs</h4><a class="anchor-link" href="#network-session-logs"><span aria-hidden="true" class="anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path fill="currentcolor" d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42Zm8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33ZM8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 1.1.22 1 1 0 0 0 .32-.22l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42Z"></path></svg></span></a></div> <p>The <code>zero_trust_network_sessions</code> dataset, available through <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/insights/logs/logpush/">Logpush</a>, includes the following fields:</p> <div class="table-scroll" tabindex="0" role="region" aria-label="Table"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Field</th> <th>Description</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><code>OnrampType</code></td> <td>How the session entered Cloudflare One. Values: <code>CF1_CLIENT</code>, <code>MESH</code>, <code>WORKERS_VPC</code>, <code>MAGIC</code>, <code>OTHER</code>.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>Offramp</code></td> <td>Where the session was routed. Sessions routed to a Mesh node report <code>MESH</code>.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>SourceName</code></td> <td>Name of the Worker that started the session. Only populated for Workers VPC sessions.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>SourceID</code></td> <td>Stable identifier of the Worker that started the session. Only populated for Workers VPC sessions.</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>DestinationReplicaID</code></td> <td>The replica that served the session, such as a specific replica of a Mesh node or a <code>cloudflared</code> replica of a Cloudflare Tunnel.</td> </tr> </tbody> </table></div> <p>For example, <code>OnrampType = 'WORKERS_VPC' AND Offramp = 'MESH'</code> returns every session where a Worker reached a service behind a Mesh node, and <code>SourceName</code> tells you which Worker it was.</p> <aside role="note" aria-label="Redeploy your Workers" class="aside-card flex items-start gap-3 rounded-lg px-4 py-3 my-4" style="--_c: var(--nb-warning); --_t: var(--nb-warning-muted);" data-astro-cid-znle5jil><span class="flex h-[1.375em] shrink-0 items-center" aria-hidden="true" data-astro-cid-znle5jil><svg width="1em" height="1em" viewBox="0 0 256 256" class="h-[1em] w-[1em]" data-astro-cid-znle5jil="true" data-icon="ph:warning"><path fill="currentColor" d="M236.8 188.09L149.35 36.22a24.76 24.76 0 0 0-42.7 0L19.2 188.09a23.51 23.51 0 0 0 0 23.72A24.35 24.35 0 0 0 40.55 224h174.9a24.35 24.35 0 0 0 21.33-12.19a23.51 23.51 0 0 0 .02-23.72m-13.87 15.71a8.5 8.5 0 0 1-7.48 4.2H40.55a8.5 8.5 0 0 1-7.48-4.2a7.59 7.59 0 0 1 0-7.72l87.45-151.87a8.75 8.75 0 0 1 15 0l87.45 151.87a7.59 7.59 0 0 1-.04 7.72M120 144v-40a8 8 0 0 1 16 0v40a8 8 0 0 1-16 0m20 36a12 12 0 1 1-12-12a12 12 0 0 1 12 12"/></svg></span><div class="flex min-w-0 flex-1 flex-col gap-0.5" data-astro-cid-znle5jil><p class="m-0 text-base leading-snug font-semibold" data-astro-cid-znle5jil>Redeploy your Workers</p><div class="aside-card-body text-sm leading-normal" data-astro-cid-znle5jil><p><code>SourceName</code> and <code>SourceID</code> are only populated for Workers deployed after 29 September 2026. To include them for an existing Worker, redeploy it — for example, with <code>npx wrangler deploy</code>. No code changes are required.</p></div></div></aside> <div tabindex="-1" class="heading-wrapper level-h4"><h4 id="see-which-tunnel-and-replica-received-a-session">See which tunnel and replica received a session</h4><a class="anchor-link" href="#see-which-tunnel-and-replica-received-a-session"><span aria-hidden="true" class="anchor-icon"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path fill="currentcolor" d="m12.11 15.39-3.88 3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1-3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0-3.5l3.88-3.88a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-3.88 3.89a4.48 4.48 0 0 0 6.33 6.33l3.89-3.88a1 1 0 1 0-1.42-1.42Zm8.58-12.08a4.49 4.49 0 0 0-6.33 0l-3.89 3.88a1 1 0 0 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.88a2.52 2.52 0 0 1 3.5 0 2.47 2.47 0 0 1 0 3.5l-3.88 3.88a1 1 0 1 0 1.42 1.42l3.88-3.89a4.49 4.49 0 0 0 0-6.33ZM8.83 15.17a1 1 0 0 0 1.1.22 1 1 0 0 0 .32-.22l4.92-4.92a1 1 0 0 0-1.42-1.42l-4.92 4.92a1 1 0 0 0 0 1.42Z"></path></svg></span></a></div> <p>With <code>DestinationReplicaID</code>, you can now confirm which <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/tunnel/">Cloudflare Tunnel</a> and which <code>cloudflared</code> replica received traffic for a specific session. Combine it with the existing <code>DestinationTunnelID</code> field to trace a session to an exact tunnel replica — or Mesh node replica — when you run multiple replicas for high availability. The replica ID matches the <strong>Connector ID</strong> shown in the dashboard, so you can <a href="https://developers.cloudflare.com/tunnel/observability/#remote-log-streaming">stream that replica's logs</a> with <code>cloudflared tail --connector-id</code>.</p> <p>Sessions logged before this change are not backfilled. If your Worker answers <code>304 Not Modified</code>, the cache keeps the stored body. If your Worker answers with a full <code>200</code> response, that response replaces the cached one.</p> <p><code>invalidate()</code> accepts the same options as <code>purge()</code>: <code>tags</code>, <code>pathPrefixes</code>, or <code>purgeEverything</code>. It follows the same per-entrypoint scoping and resolves to the same result object. Call it as <code>ctx.cache.invalidate()</code>, or import <code>cache</code> from <code>cloudflare:workers</code> and call <code>cache.invalidate()</code>.</p> <p>Use <code>invalidate()</code> when one call covers many cached responses but only some of them changed. Your Worker needs to emit <code>ETag</code> or <code>Last-Modified</code> and answer matching conditional requests with <code>304</code>. Each unchanged response then costs a validator check instead of a full regeneration:</p> <div><div data-nb-tabs data-nb-sync-key="workersExamples" class><div class="relative flex border-b
